question: Which of the following most often causes cholestatic jaundice:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Erythromycin estolate" -> "known to cause cholestatic jaundice" -> "inhibits bile flow" -> "increased bilirubin levels" -> 85%
CHAIN: "INH" -> "associated with hepatotoxicity" -> "can cause jaundice" -> "not primarily cholestatic" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Pyrazinamide" -> "can cause liver dysfunction" -> "may lead to jaundice" -> "not specifically cholestatic" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Ethionamide" -> "can cause liver toxicity" -> "may result in jaundice" -> "not commonly cholestatic" -> 60%
analysis: Cholestatic jaundice is often associated with drug-induced liver injury, particularly with certain antibiotics and antitubercular agents. Among the options provided, Erythromycin estolate is well-documented to cause cholestatic jaundice due to its effects on bile flow and liver function. INH, Pyrazinamide, and Ethionamide can also cause liver toxicity, but they are less commonly associated with cholestatic jaundice specifically compared to Erythromycin estolate. Therefore, based on the known pharmacological effects and the literature, Erythromycin estolate is the most likely cause of cholestatic jaundice in this context.
